question: Which main nerve links the gastrointestinal tract directly to the brain?
explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary communication highway connecting your gut and your brain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: Why is the gut often called our second brain regarding mood?

options.A: It prevents all forms of physical inflammation
options.B: It directly digests complex psychiatric medications
options.C: It completely replaces the function of the brain
options.D: It produces most of the body's serotonin supply

explanation: Correct! Specialized cells and microbes in your gut manufacture a large share of your body's serotonin, directly influencing your mood. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: A patient with severe schizophrenia is losing weight because they never cook or buy groceries. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: A physical inability to chew or swallow solid food
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard grocery store items
options.C: Negative symptoms like apathy and lack of drive
options.D: A deliberate choice to fast for religious reasons

explanation: Well done! Negative symptoms such as avolition can rob patients of the motivation needed to plan and execute daily tasks like cooking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?
explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: Why do patients taking lithium need careful guidance about their salt and water intake?

options.A: Salt completely destroys the chemical structure of the lithium pill
options.B: Lithium alters fluid balance and can easily reach toxic levels if hydration shifts
options.C: Water causes lithium to instantly evaporate inside the human stomach
options.D: Patients on lithium lose all sense of taste for salty foods

explanation: Spot on! Lithium handles similarly to sodium in the kidneys, so dehydration or sudden salt changes can dangerously spike drug levels. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: Which lab tests are most important when starting a patient on an antipsychotic known for metabolic side effects?

options.A: Direct measurement of brain wave activity
options.B: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
options.C: Routine throat swab for bacterial culture

explanation: Correct! Because these drugs can disrupt blood sugar and fats, keeping an eye on glucose and lipid levels is essential. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: A depressed patient has lost ten pounds, looks pale, and is fatigued. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Assume the weight loss is normal for depression and take no action
options.B: Perform a comprehensive nutritional assessment including a diet history and labs
options.C: Recommend an intense physical fitness gym membership to build muscle
options.D: Tell the patient to immediately start eating three large meals a day

explanation: Well done! A structured assessment helps us uncover specific nutritional deficits and physical health risks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Why do we generally recommend complex carbohydrates over simple sugars for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They prevent the dramatic energy crashes that can worsen mood swings
options.B: They taste much sweeter and satisfy cravings instantly
options.C: They require no digestion and enter the bloodstream immediately
options.D: They completely cure all forms of clinical depression overnight

explanation: Correct! Complex carbs digest slowly, keeping blood sugar and energy levels stable throughout the day. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: What common physical issue can mild dehydration often mimic in a psychiatric patient?

options.A: Rapid hair loss and brittle fingernails
options.B: Sudden weight gain and high blood pressure
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of hearing

explanation: Spot on! Not drinking enough water frequently presents as brain fog, tiredness, and heightened nervous tension. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: Which food must be strictly avoided by a patient taking a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)?
explanation: You got it! These foods are high in tyramine, which can trigger a dangerous, life-threatening spike in blood pressure when combined with MAOIs. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What is the main goal of recommending an anti-inflammatory diet, like the Mediterranean diet, in psychiatric care?

options.A: To force the body to rapidly lose large amounts of water weight
options.B: To cure genetic disorders within a few weeks of starting
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any prescription medications
options.D: To reduce systemic inflammation that negatively impacts brain function

explanation: Correct! Lowering bodily inflammation helps support optimal brain health and can ease depressive symptoms. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What is a practical, budget-friendly nursing tip for a patient who cannot afford fresh vegetables?

options.A: Advise them to forage for wild plants in local public parks
options.B: Telling them to skip vegetables entirely until they find more money
options.C: Suggesting nutritious frozen vegetables or rinsed canned options
options.D: Insisting they only buy organic produce from specialty markets

explanation: Well done! Frozen and canned veggies are affordable, last longer, and still offer great nutrition when money is tight. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthy eating for vulnerable psychiatric patients?

options.A: An overabundance of free local community gardens
options.B: Financial poverty and limited access to grocery stores
options.C: Living in an area classified as a food desert

explanation: Spot on! Poverty and poor access are major hurdles, whereas having plenty of community gardens would actually help people get fresh food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: Why is the nurse considered the central link in nutritional care for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They hold the legal authority to prescribe all specialized diets
options.B: They are the only team members trained in human biology
options.C: They dictate what medications the psychiatrist must order
options.D: They spend the most time with the patient and monitor daily habits

explanation: Correct! Because nurses are constantly around patients, they are in the best position to track real-time food intake and side effects. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h8)

question: A patient on a new psychiatric drug is refusing to eat due to severe dry mouth. Who should the nurse consult first?

options.A: The medical records coding and billing department
options.B: The registered dietitian and the prescribing psychiatrist
options.C: The hospital maintenance and facility management team
options.D: The security personnel assigned to the psychiatric unit

explanation: You got it! A dietitian can help modify food textures for dry mouth, while the psychiatrist can review the medication dosage. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h8)
